zucchini-noodles-pesto.headnote: Zucchini noodles only need a few minutes in the pan. Stop while the strands still have some bite, then take them off the heat before tossing with pesto so the sauce stays bright and the zucchini does not turn watery.
zucchini-noodles-pesto.substitutions: No pesto? Toss the zucchini with olive oil, parmesan, lemon, and black pepper instead. Yellow summer squash can replace the zucchini; keep the same short cooking time and stop before the strands soften completely.
zucchini-noodles-pesto.storage: Zucchini noodles are best eaten right away because they release water as they sit. If needed, refrigerate leftovers for one day and reheat briefly in a dry pan, then add a fresh spoonful of pesto after warming.

antipasto-skewers.headnote: Keep the mozzarella, tomatoes, olives, and cured meat close in size so each skewer has a balanced bite. Drain wet ingredients well before assembly, then finish with olive oil, black pepper, and basil just before serving.
antipasto-skewers.substitutions: Use any combination of small mozzarella balls, firm cheese cubes, olives, cherry tomatoes, marinated artichokes, roasted peppers, or folded salami. Keep the pieces bite-size and choose a mix of creamy, briny, and fresh ingredients.
antipasto-skewers.storage: Assemble these as close to serving as possible. If making them ahead, refrigerate covered for up to one day and add basil, olive oil, and any balsamic finish just before eating so the herbs stay fresh.

baked-feta-pasta.substitutions: Rigatoni, penne, fusilli, or another short pasta all work. If cherry tomatoes are unavailable, use grape tomatoes or chopped ripe plum tomatoes; if replacing feta, choose another tangy cheese that softens well rather than a hard grating cheese.
baked-feta-pasta.storage: Refrigerate leftovers in a sealed container for up to two days. Reheat gently with a splash of water until the sauce loosens, then add fresh basil after warming.

gnocchi-pesto-cherry-tomatoes.headnote: Cook the gnocchi until they float, then give them a minute in the pan so the edges pick up a little color. Add pesto off the heat and fold in the tomatoes last so the sauce stays green and the tomatoes keep some shape.
gnocchi-pesto-cherry-tomatoes.substitutions: Shelf-stable or refrigerated potato gnocchi both work. Sun-dried tomatoes can replace the cherry tomatoes for a more concentrated flavor, and a spoonful of ricotta can soften a very strong pesto.
gnocchi-pesto-cherry-tomatoes.storage: Refrigerate leftovers for up to two days. Reheat gently in a skillet with a teaspoon of water, then stir in a small spoonful of fresh pesto after the gnocchi are hot.
